summary: River City Bangkok is a riverside arts and antiques centre in Si Phraya, with rotating gallery exhibitions, events, auctions, shops and eateries. It works well as a flexible stop on a Chao Phraya or Talat Noi day; choose it for the exhibitions actually running on your dates, since the programme changes frequently.
whyGo: Browse changing contemporary art exhibitions and antiques under one roof, with the riverfront and Si Phraya Pier immediately outside.
Combine a gallery visit with a public boat ride, nearby Talat Noi lanes, or a meal by the river.
bestFor: Art and antiques browsing without committing to a full museum day.
A rainy-day or heat break between riverside neighbourhood visits.
Travellers who enjoy choosing a visit around a specific current exhibition or event.
skipIf: You want a permanent, comprehensive museum collection or guaranteed December exhibition.
You need confirmed step-free access details; the venue’s visitor information does not spell these out.
duration: Allow about 1–2 hours for a casual gallery-and-riverfront visit; this is a planning estimate and varies with the exhibitions, shops and dining you choose.
cost: Venue entry is not listed as ticketed on the visitor page; individual exhibitions or events may have separate terms. Many past exhibitions were advertised as free, but confirm the specific December listing before going. Public boat fares vary by route; the venue lists BTS single fares at THB 15–62 and MRT at THB 17–45.
hours: Official visitor information lists daily hours, including weekends and public holidays, as 10:00–20:00. Confirm any individual gallery or event hours before visiting.
bestTime: Go on a weekday or earlier in the day for a quieter browse. For a riverfront atmosphere, arrive later in the afternoon, allowing enough time before the 20:00 close. These are practical suggestions, not venue-published crowd forecasts.
gettingThere: The address is 23 Charoen Krung Soi 24, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong. Thai Smile Boat Purple and Green lines stop at River City Pier 3; yellow, orange and green-flag public boats stop at Si Phraya Pier. From BTS Saphan Taksin, take the public boat from Sathorn Pier to Si Phraya. From MRT Hua Lamphong, the venue suggests taxi/tuk-tuk or buses 1, 75 or 35. Bus routes 36, 45, 93 and 187 also serve the area. Check live route operations before setting out.
booking: No advance booking is indicated for general visits. Check the official What’s On page for dated exhibitions, events, films, music and auction details; book only if the specific listing requires it. Call +66 2 237 0077 if details remain unclear.
accessibility: The official visit page gives transport and parking information but no detailed wheelchair, lift, toilet or sensory-access information. Contact the venue in advance on +66 2 237 0077 to confirm the route and facilities you need.
practicalTips: Check the official What’s On listings shortly before your visit; the page currently shows October–November 2026 listings and does not establish a December programme.
Allow time to enjoy the riverfront and use the pier, but verify boat routes and operating times on the day.
Parking is available on site; the venue lists 30 minutes free without a stamp, then THB 40 per hour or fraction. With a stamp it lists three hours free, then THB 40 per hour from the fourth hour.
Pets are not allowed inside the venue, according to its visitor policy.
decemberNotes: December 2026 exhibitions, events and holiday opening changes were not confirmed on the live listings checked on 17 October 2026; currently displayed events end in November. Recheck the official What’s On and Plan Your Visit pages near your travel date. Bangkok’s December riverside evenings can be busy, so leave extra time if connecting with a boat or dinner plan; this is general planning advice, not a published venue forecast.
uncertainties: December 2026 exhibition and event schedule is not yet listed in the checked official calendar.
Admission terms can vary by exhibition or event; no general ticket price is published on the visitor page.
Detailed accessibility provisions are not described in the official visitor information.
Boat lines, fares and timetables can change; confirm current service before travel.
